Title: Fast ECoT: Fast Embodied Chain-of-Thought via Cross-Step Plan Reuse, Modular Parallelism and Asynchronous Scheduling

Title: VLA-Cache: Efficient Vision-Language-Action Inference via Token-Level Cross-Frame Caching
Primary Metric: Success vs cache hit-rate; ablation on gripper/object tokens vs background
Key Mechanism: (1) Static visual KV cache; (2) Shows 'static-looking' != 'safe to cache' for gripper/objects; (3) Task-relevant token refresh
Relevance to BudgetLoop-VLA: Refresh mode = VLA-Cache selective refresh policy applied to grounded CoT; Reflex mode = full VLA-Cache visual + action bypass
Gaps BudgetLoop Exploits: VLA-Cache saves compute and discards it — BudgetLoop banks it; VLA-Cache does not model compute budget across steps — we do

Title: EfficientVLA: Joint Language Layer Pruning, Visual Token Selection and Action Head Caching
Method Category: Joint: LLM prune + Vision select + Action cache

Title: ActionCache: Flow-Based Action Head Warm-Start from Historical Intermediate Actions
Reported Speedup: π0: up to 11.75×; GR00T-N1.6: up to 34.43× on action-head
Key Mechanism: (1) Stores historical intermediate action trajectories; (2) Flow-based alignment to current step observation; (3) Warm-starts diffusion / flow-matching action head
Relevance to BudgetLoop-VLA: Reflex mode can plug ActionCache as action bypass; Deliberate mode disables cache and runs full action head
Gaps BudgetLoop Exploits: ActionCache accelerates but does not coordinate with vision/CoT caches; no joint budget controller

Title: ElegantVLA: When Is Full Reasoning Worth It? Dynamic Scheduling across Vision, LLM and Action Head
Primary Metric: Accuracy-efficiency Pareto; fraction of steps running full sub-modules
Key Mechanism: (1) Separate cheap difficulty scorers per modality; (2) Per-step choose full vs lightweight vision / LLM / action; (3) Heuristic scheduler, no bank
Relevance to BudgetLoop-VLA: ElegantVLA = closest existing compute allocator; our P3 direct comparison baseline #1
Gaps BudgetLoop Exploits: ElegantVLA has no compute bank (b_t); no forced latency ceiling; no loop module; no grounded-vs-semantic TTL split
Notes: Most important comparison baseline for 'allocator' claim

Title: ERVLA: An Empirical Study of Explicit Chain-of-Thought in Vision-Language-Action Models
Method Category: Empirical Analysis of CoT in VLAs
Primary Metric: CoT-usage ablations; grounded guidance vs semantic-only; error accumulation
Key Mechanism: (1) High-level semantic reasoning alone has small gain; (2) Grounded guidance (move/gripper/objects) directly coupled to actions has big gain; (3) Using explicit CoT as action prefix causes error accumulation
Relevance to BudgetLoop-VLA: Foundational justification for our CoT-level TTL split: goal/subtask long-TTL; move/gripper/objects short-TTL; immediate-invalidation on contact
Gaps BudgetLoop Exploits: ERVLA says don't cache entire CoT — we exactly implement that partition
Notes: User seed paper #4 (motivates TTL-tiered cache policy)

Title: OpenVLA: An Open-Source Vision-Language-Action Model

Relevance to BudgetLoop-VLA: All experiments in this track run on OpenVLA (or ECoT-finetuned variant) as the base model

Title: ECoT: Embodied Chain of Thought

Relevance to BudgetLoop-VLA: Base architecture manipulated by every method in this track; BudgetLoop modes = tiered reuse of ECoT's modules
Gaps BudgetLoop Exploits: ECoT is trained; this track is training-free so we must operate frozen

Title: Mixture-of-Recursions: Learning Dynamic Recursive Depths for Adaptive Token-Level Computation
Reported Speedup: Up to ~2× compute reduction on hard tokens
Primary Metric: Accuracy vs compute; token-wise recursion depth distribution
Key Mechanism: (1) Router per token decides recursion depth {1..K}; (2) Shares transformer weights across recursions; (3) End-to-end trained router + main model
Relevance to BudgetLoop-VLA: Inspiration ONLY — our Deliberate-mode token-selective recursion approximates MoR without training
Gaps BudgetLoop Exploits: MoR requires training router — forbidden in training-free setting; our approximation via hidden residual entropy proxy is novel
Notes: Direct training-style upper bound for token-selective Deliberate mode

Title: Hyperloop Transformers: Begin-Middle-End Architecture with Looped Middle Blocks for Fixed Parameter Budget Efficiency
Training-Free?: NO (architecture trained from scratch with loop)
Reported Speedup: Same params → better accuracy OR same accuracy → fewer params
Primary Metric: Accuracy vs param storage vs FLOPs
Key Mechanism: (1) Begin + Middle × K loops + End; (2) Middle weights shared across K iterations; (3) Trained from scratch with loop-aware init
Relevance to BudgetLoop-VLA: Direct justification for '1B param storage budget, loop = better effective depth than 1B non-loop' claim
Gaps BudgetLoop Exploits: Hyperloop is trained with loop — we loop frozen plain checkpoints → representation drift risk; Hyperloop no dynamic K per step
Notes: Training-style architectural upper bound for Deliberate-mode K=2 loop

Title: Training-Free Looped Transformers: Damped Small-Step Recursion on Frozen Mid-Stack Layers
Primary Metric: Accuracy vs FLOPs; hidden-norm residual convergence; naive loop degradation
Key Mechanism: (1) Loop only continuous mid-stack window; (2) Small K ∈ {2,3}; (3) Damping α h' = α h_loop + (1-α) h_prev; (4) Naive loop hurts → damping required
Relevance to BudgetLoop-VLA: EXACT blueprint for Deliberate-mode K loop P2 experiments; our P2 directly sweeps mid-stack window / K / α / naive vs damped
Gaps BudgetLoop Exploits: Does not operate on VLAs; does not combine with caching; no per-step difficulty gating; no compute bank

Title: LoopQ: On Loop-Dependent Activation Drift and Recursive Quantization Error in Looped Transformers
Primary Metric: Activation norm drift across loops; W4A8 / INT4 recursive error; perplexity collapse
Key Mechanism: (1) Same shared weights iterated → activation drift accumulates per loop; (2) Low-bit quantization → recursive rounding error compounds; (3) LoopQ-specific correction shifts
Relevance to BudgetLoop-VLA: Hard constraint on our Deliberate mode: if run quantized, max K=2 + must check hidden norm; if divergence → rollback to K=1
Gaps BudgetLoop Exploits: Our claim must NOT say 'loop always helps' — we acknowledge LoopQ pathology with fallback + K=2 cap only in Deliberate
Notes: Limits / failure mode reference for loop claim

Title: RD-VLA: Recurrent Decoding Vision-Language-Action with Adaptive Stop
Training-Free?: NO — TBPTT trains recurrent action head
Reported Speedup: Latency reduction via early stop on easy steps; better on hard tasks
Primary Metric: Task success; action-head KL; p95 latency
Key Mechanism: (1) Recurrent action head with TBPTT; (2) Adaptive stop token decides when to halt action refinement
Relevance to BudgetLoop-VLA: Training-style upper bound only; our K=2 action refinement loop is training-free approximation of RD-VLA's recurrent refinement
Gaps BudgetLoop Exploits: Cannot claim training-free parity with RD-VLA; treat as theoretical ceiling; ours is training-free proxy

Title: Looped Transformers Are Better In-Context Learners

Relevance to BudgetLoop-VLA: Supports '1B loop > 1B non-loop at same storage' but limited to ICL; we extend to frozen VLA inference with caveats
Gaps BudgetLoop Exploits: Does not address VLAs or training-free on frozen checkpoints

Reported Speedup: Hard latency ceiling at all times
